$comment: Canonical registry of cross-SDK behaviours. Each SDK's conformance runner
executes the scenarios listed for it and writes report-<sdk>.json; check.py
then fails the build if a runner skipped or omitted one it is declared to
`sdks` is the contract, not an aspiration: it lists the SDKs that implement
the scenario TODAY. Parity gaps live in `missing_from` with a reason, so a
gap is a tracked fact rather than silence. Closing a gap means moving the
SDK from `missing_from` into `sdks` — after which the gate enforces it.

scenarios.description: insert, get, find by filter, update, count, delete; deleting twice is an error
insert_many returns ids in input order
upsert embeddings, search returns the nearest doc first with ascending distance
an embedding of the wrong dimension is rejected before touching the database
enqueue returns a positive job id and stats.available reflects it
insert points, within_radius filters by distance, nearest ranks by proximity
issue a PostgREST JWT carrying the tenant role and sidecar url
connecting to a project with no migrations applied fails with a clear error
with_user scopes reads and writes to one user under a FORCE RLS policy

missing_from.ts: TypeScript SDK has no withUser; tracked in CHANGELOG known limitations

scenarios.description: subscribe receives an insert event for the project's schema

missing_from.py: Python SDK has no subscribe; would need a websocket dependency

scenarios.description: register a matview, refresh it, and read last_refresh_at back

missing_from.ts: TypeScript SDK has no matview helper
missing_from.py: Python SDK has no matview helper
